records.name: Philadelphia Veterans Parade and Festival
records.summary: A yearly parade and street festival on the Ben Franklin Parkway that honors veterans. Veterans started it about 12 years ago, and bands, groups and organizations can apply to march in it or run a table at the festival.
records.what_you_do: Groups and organizations apply through one online form to march in the parade, run a festival table, or both. The approved participant page also names individual veterans as possible registrants. Anyone can come watch the parade and visit the festival.

schedule.text: Held once a year in the fall, on a Sunday. The parade starts around noon on the Ben Franklin Parkway and ends at Eakins Oval, where the festival follows.

locations.label: Ben Franklin Parkway to Eakins Oval

cost.text: The parade and festival pages do not list a fee to watch, to march, or to run a table.

first_step.how: Come watch the parade on the Ben Franklin Parkway at noon, or apply online by October 21, 2026 to march or run a festival table.
first_step.basis: Watching is open to anyone with no sign-up, and marching or running a table needs an application that the organizers approve.
first_step.what_to_expect: Watching means finding a spot along the Ben Franklin Parkway for the noon start. The parade ends at Eakins Oval, where the festival ran from 12:30 to 3:30 pm in 2026. Approved groups get their own staging times, and marchers are asked to arrive between 10:30 and 11 am.
first_visit_tips: The parade is televised on Channel 6 if you would rather watch from home.
Approved groups should follow their own staging times, which differ by vehicle type.
Send questions about an application to the contact named on the approved participant page, since the site has no phone number.

records.notes: Schedule rewritten from a one-time date to the yearly pattern, since one-time dates stay out of schedule text. The October 21, 2026 application deadline is in first_step and will go stale; re-check after that date. The late-season post is dated September 24, 2026 on the page. Staff contacts on the About page are listed by role; individual staff emails are not recorded. The site states no eligibility rule or approval standard. Organizations named as examples on the participant page (American Legion, VFW) are in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Voices of Pride
records.summary: An LGBTQ and ally mixed voice chorus in Philadelphia that holds two audition windows a year and also welcomes non-singing members.
records.what_you_do: Audition to sing with the chorus, or join as a non-singing member, by emailing the membership team. Rehearsals are on Tuesday nights in Center City. The chorus also has a table at public events where members sign people up for auditions.

schedule.text: Rehearsals run on Tuesday nights at Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S 17th St. Singers audition twice a year, in summer (August) and winter (January).

cost.text: The join page and home page list no dues or fees. The site has a donation link.

first_step.how: Email membership@pvop.org to sign up for an audition, or to join as a non-singing member.
first_step.basis: There is a clear, low-bar way in by email, no training is required, and non-singers can join too. Singing members still need the audition.
first_step.what_to_expect: Rehearsals are on Tuesday nights at Resurrection Philadelphia in Center City. The join page gives no start time and does not say how long a rehearsal runs, so ask by email first. Singers must audition before they join, and the site lists no dues or fees.
first_visit_tips: Email membership@pvop.org before you come, since the site does not give rehearsal start times.
Prepared music is optional at the audition, so you do not need to learn a piece first.
Stop by the PVOP table at a public event such as the Philly Pride Festival or OURFest, where members sign people up for auditions.

records.notes: Batch file lists kind club; the group file says nonprofit. Kept nonprofit, flag for the importer. The join page gives a Tuesday August audition at 6 pm with no year, so it is not in schedule text. One search result mentioned a late August 2026 round, and older listings name William Way Community Center; neither appears on the group's own pages, so neither is used. Confirm the rehearsal place by email before a first visit. Only English text was seen, so languages are left out. Sign of life moved to June 2026 on the June 30, 2026 Pride concert listing. The OURFest listing on October 11, 2026 is upcoming and is noted in tips.

records.name: Philadelphia Wind Symphony
records.summary: A volunteer band of about 51 woodwind, brass, and percussion players who perform five or six concerts a season across Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Apply as a substitute if you play wind, brass or percussion, or hear the band at one of its public concerts. Donations and newsletter sign-up are also open on the site.

schedule.text: Concerts run from fall through early summer, at a range of venues. Before each concert the volunteer players rehearse three or four times over two weeks, with no set weekday.

cost.text: The concerts page lists no ticket prices for most concerts. The band describes its Halloween family concert as free.

first_step.how: If you play wind, brass or percussion, submit the online substitute musician application, which asks for your date of birth, a one-page resume and playing videos.
first_step.basis: Regular seats are closed for the 2026 to 2027 season, and substitutes must send an online application with a resume and videos, so there is no walk-in way in. The public can still attend concerts.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public concerts are the easiest way to hear the band first. The site does not say what a substitute's first rehearsal is like, but rehearsals are a few volunteer sessions in the two weeks before each concert.
first_visit_tips: Check the concerts page for each concert's venue and time, since they change from one concert to the next.
Have playing videos ready that show both a fast technical piece and a slow lyrical one, because the application asks for both.
Email the band to ask for the rehearsal schedule, since the site lists no rehearsal times or place.

records.notes: The season field is left out because concerts run from fall to early summer, which the season list cannot express. The October concert page prints no year and its link says 2025, so last_sign_of_life keeps the tier 1 value of 2025-10. The June concert page says details are coming and gives no year beyond the season label, so it is not used as evidence. One concert is listed at Bryn Mawr College, outside the city. Summary changed from about six concerts to five or six, based on the five concerts on the 2026 to 2027 page. The 'about 51 players' figure is from tier 1 and was not on the pages read this session. The partner band named on the concerts page is in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Woodworks
records.summary: A woodshop in Philadelphia where beginners and experienced woodworkers take classes, use the shop with a membership, and send kids to workshops and summer camps.
records.what_you_do: Take a one-day or evening class, learn the tools in an intro session, or join as a shop member. New members complete a safety certification before using the shop. There is a women-only shop introduction.

schedule.text: Classes meet mostly during the day, with some evening sessions, on several days a week. The shop is closed on Mondays, and members can use it Tuesday through Sunday.

cost.text: Unlimited membership is $169 a month, month to month after an initial commitment, and new members also pay $299 for the safety certification. Class prices are set per class; for example, a one-day women's intro lists $239 tuition plus $79 for materials.

access.notes: The nearest SEPTA stop, Ivy Ridge, is directly across from the shop, according to the members shop page.

first_step.how: Sign up for a beginner class on the class calendar. Classes do not need a membership.
first_step.basis: The shop lists several intro sessions for beginners and says classes need no membership or safety certification, but the site does not describe drop in visits.
first_step.what_to_expect: A full-day intro class runs about eight hours, with an instructor, on the shop's professional tools. The women's intro includes a cutting board made from rough lumber in the morning and turning on a lathe in the afternoon, and you take home several finished pieces. Materials cost extra on top of tuition.
first_visit_tips: Plan for a full day, since the intro classes run about eight hours. The class page does not say whether lunch is included, so ask when you call.
The shop has private off-street parking, and the Ivy Ridge SEPTA stop is across the street.
You can reschedule a class only if you ask at least 14 days before it starts.
Call (267) 331-5880 or email the shop to ask what to bring or wear, since the class pages do not say.

records.notes: Shop hours corrected: the calendar shows Mondays closed, and the members page says members have access Tuesday through Sunday, which includes Friday. Tier 1 said Fridays were closed. Summary changed from after-school programs to the kids workshops and summer camps the page names. Fall sale discounts are left out of cost because they are a one-time promotion. Judgement flag: this is a paid membership shop. Kept publish because it runs beginner classes, a women's intro and kids programs, and rule 4 hides businesses with no community program. Drop in for non-members and wheelchair access are not stated.

records.name: Philadelphia Young Playwrights
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings playwriting to young people through classes, school programs and a yearly playwriting festival. It also stages showcases and productions of young writers' work.
records.what_you_do: Join a free Out of School Time workshop for Philadelphia students, or a one-day Day Off camp. Students can also submit a play to the annual playwriting festival (the 2026 deadline was June 1, 2026) and can attend performances in the 2026 to 2027 season. Volunteering and membership are not listed.

schedule.text: Out of School Time workshops run in several rounds during the school year, usually on Wednesdays or Saturdays for four to six weeks. Day Off camps are single full-day workshops.

locations.label: Workshop sites include the Asian Arts Initiative, the Philadelphia Museum of Art and The Rotunda

cost.text: Out of School Time workshops are free for Philadelphia students. Festival submissions are free for Philadelphia students and cost $10 for students outside the city, with free codes for past program participants and a request form for families who cannot pay.

first_step.how: Pick a free Out of School Time workshop for Philadelphia students and register through its sign-up link, or call 215-665-9226 with questions.
first_step.basis: Several workshops are listed for beginners or for all levels, each has a sign-up link, and the programs are free for Philadelphia students. The site does not describe drop in visits.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most workshops meet on Wednesdays or Saturdays for four to six weeks, and the Day Off camps are one full day each. Students go from a first idea to a first draft, and the Duchamp workshop has its monologues performed by professional actors. The programs cost nothing for Philadelphia students, and the site does not list start times.
first_visit_tips: Start times are not listed on the program pages, so call 215-665-9226 before you plan the trip.
Workshops meet at different sites, including the Asian Arts Initiative, the Philadelphia Museum of Art and The Rotunda, so check the location for your program.
The office is on the second floor at 1219 Vine Street if you need to visit in person. The site lists no office hours.

records.notes: The Day Off camp dates are printed without years; the years come from the registration link, so they are not written in the record. The festival submission deadline of June 1, 2026 has passed. Status moved from probably_active to active on that dated deadline. The contact page email is obfuscated and is left out. Asian Arts Initiative is named as a workshop site and is in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Choral Ensembles
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs youth choirs for boys, girls and a combined group, along with instrument and music classes. Its choirs hold public concerts across the year.
records.what_you_do: Audition for one of the three choirs: the Philadelphia Boys Choir and Chorale, the Philadelphia Girls Choir, or the Commonwealth Youth Choir. Each has its own audition booking page for the 2026 to 2027 season. You can also take private lessons or musicianship classes, or attend a public concert.

schedule.text: Choirs hold auditions each season and then place singers in age-based ensembles. Semesters end with a joint concert for family and friends, and the choirs perform in public through the year.

locations.label: Philadelphia Boys Choir and Girls Choir audition site, also the mailing address

cost.text: The pages reviewed list no tuition, fees, or audition charge.

first_step.how: Open the audition page for the choir that fits your child, linked from the Auditions menu, and book an audition for the 2026 to 2027 season.
first_step.basis: Joining a choir takes an audition, so families learn what a choir is like only after auditioning. Auditions are open for the 2026 to 2027 season.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each choir has its own audition booking page, and the auditions landing page does not say how long an audition lasts or what to prepare. The girls choir places singers in ensembles by age and skill after the audition, so a child joins a group that fits their level. Public concerts are a way to hear the choirs first.
first_visit_tips: Book at the right audition site: the boys and girls choirs audition at 1336 Spring Garden Street, and the Commonwealth Youth Choir at 8855 Germantown Avenue.
Find Your Instrument is run with partner schools, so ask your child's music teacher about it rather than signing up directly.
Call 215-222-3500 or email info@pycemusic.org to ask about tuition, since the pages do not list it.

records.notes: The placeholder contact name 'The Organization' from tier 1 is removed. Find Your Instrument works with partner schools and their music teachers, not individual families, so what_you_do says so. Choirs run in semesters, so no season value fits and recurring is set to true; days and times are left out because the only dated items were one-time events. The 2026 years on the concert listings are not printed next to the dates (the site shows only a 2026 copyright), so last_sign_of_life keeps the tier 1 value of 2026-10 and may need correcting. Rehearsal days and times are not on the site. The three choirs' own audition pages and the lessons page were not opened, because of the six-fetch budget for this group. The Commonwealth Youth Choir was formed in 2024 from two earlier groups, per the programs page.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Dance Fest
records.summary: A festival that brings young dancers together for three days of master classes and a chance to perform. It runs in Philadelphia and in the Lehigh Valley.
records.what_you_do: Dance companies apply through an online form and pay a $50 company fee, then submit up to two pieces for review. Each company performs one piece of up to 4.5 minutes, and each dancer takes four to six master classes. Scholarship audition classes are held at each festival.

schedule.text: Two festivals each spring: a Philadelphia weekend at Drexel University and a Lehigh Valley weekend at Muhlenberg College. Each has an optional Friday class, Saturday master classes from 9 am to 6 pm, and Sunday classes and performances.

cost.text: Fees are set per festival: a $50 company application fee, $115 per performing dancer, $65 for a class-only dancer at the Lehigh Valley festival, or $200 for a dancer who attends both festivals.

first_step.how: Ask your dance company's director to submit the online company application and the $50 fee by November 1, 2026. Dancers then join through their company.
first_step.basis: Dancers perform only through a company that applies and pays fees, and the FAQ says non-performing dancers are wait listed at the Philadelphia festival, so there is no open walk-in path.
first_step.what_to_expect: A festival weekend is mostly master classes taught by guest teachers, with Saturday classes running from 9 am to 6 pm. Each company gets a short tech rehearsal on stage with the lighting designer before its one piece. The dancer fee covers the classes, the performance, a custom T-shirt, and photos and video of the show.
first_visit_tips: Companies submit up to two pieces for review in January, and each performing company is guaranteed one piece once the festival selects it.
Credit card payments carry a 3 percent processing fee; checks are the other option.
Dancer registration forms and the participation fee are due by February 12, 2027.
Email philayouthdancefest@gmail.com to ask about the waitlist for dancers who are not performing.

records.notes: Festival dates are the 2027 dates written on the group's pages, and they are kept out of schedule text. The scholarship audition dates on the page have no printed year (inferred 2026), so they are left out. Individual dancers without a company have no performing route; the only non-company entry in the FAQ is the Lehigh Valley class-only option. The Lehigh Valley location is marked not in city (Muhlenberg College). The festival's mailing address for checks is left out. The company deadlines (November 1, 2026 and February 12, 2027) will go stale, so re-check after November 2026. Status moved from probably_active to active on the February 2026 scholarship deadline.
